title: Adaptive hedging and socket rotation for mixed-latency SDKs
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Customers with mixed workloads (short prompt completions + long chat streams) report tail latency spikes and high token cost due to conservative per-connection pooling and uniform retry behavior. Existing SDK defaults favor connection reuse and single-attempt streaming, which is suboptimal for bursty low-latency requests and for flows where a small fraction of requests experience long stalls.

Goal: Provide a cross-language SDK feature that combines: adaptive hedged requests for short critical calls, a socket rotation policy (lightweight recycling of sockets after a soft age or error pattern), and ergonomic streaming reconnect primitives that preserve incremental partial results and handle backpressure gracefully.

Acceptance criteria:
- Python/TS/Go SDKs export a consistent config surface for: hedging window, max-hedge-attempts, socket-rotation-age, rotation-on-error-threshold, streaming-reconnect-policy.
- Hedged requests must reduce 99th percentile latency for short RPCs by >= 25% in internal bench (mixed 80/20 short/long workload) without increasing average token cost by > 10%.
- Socket rotation should reduce connection-induced tail events (stale sockets, TCP stalls) by >= 40% in stress tests.
- Streaming reconnect API must allow replay of buffered sent bytes (client-side) and resume of partial server stream without duplicating user-visible tokens; SDKs must include examples documenting typical patterns.
- Telemetry emitted: hedged_attempts, hedged_success_latency, socket_rotations, rotation_reasons, streaming_reconnects, reconnect_failures. Labels: sdk_lang, route, model_variant.

Design summary:
1) Hedging: For short calls (< configured soft_timeout_ms), SDK starts a second hedged attempt after hedging_window_ms if the primary hasn't responded. Hedged attempts use a different connection from the pool (if available) to avoid sharing blocked sockets. Responses are deduplicated by request id at the SDK layer; first-complete wins. Default: hedging_window_ms=60, max_hedge_attempts=1 for P1 workloads. Config overridable per-route.

2) Socket rotation: Each connection has a soft_age_ms; after soft_age_ms elapses the connection is marked for rotation and will be closed after its in-flight requests complete. Rotation is also triggered when a connection reports a sequence of error patterns (consecutive idempotent write failures or read stalls). Default: soft_age_ms=300000 (5m), rotation_on_error_threshold=3. Rotation uses exponential jitter to avoid thundering herd on reconnects.

3) Streaming ergonomics: Introduce streaming-reconnect-policy with three modes: "none", "best-effort", "at-least-once-sanitized". In best-effort, SDK buffers outgoing client frames (small ring buffer) and will re-send frames after reconnect; incoming partial tokens are exposed via a consistent-progress callback emitted by SDK to user, with a resume token when available. In at-least-once-sanitized, SDK attempts server-side idempotency by sending a resume token header that the server can use to drop duplicates. SDKs ship a helper wrapper that wraps user iterators to deduplicate trivial duplicates.

Compatibility and trade-offs:
- Hedging increases concurrent load; to limit cost we only enable hedging for routes with short expected server compute. For long streams hedging stays off.
- Socket rotation may increase connection churn; we mitigate with jittered backoff and connection priming heuristics so cold-start cost is low.
- Streaming reconnect helpers will not be perfect for all server implementations; we provide opt-in mode and clear docs describing when server-side resume is required.

Implementation plan:
- Phase A (this ticket): design and core implementation in TypeScript SDK, tests, and bench harnesses. Expose config surface and default values. Add telemetry counters and dashboards.
- Phase B: port to Python and Go, add language-specific ergonomic wrappers (async iterator helpers for Python, channel-friendly API for Go). Add multi-language examples in repo/examples/hedging-and-rotation.
- Phase C: public docs, migration guide, and gradual rollout (opt-in via feature flag then default-on for specific routes). Add qa gating in CI and chaos tests in staging.

Telemetry & metrics:
- Counters: hedged_attempts_total, hedged_win_total, hedged_latency_ms_p50/95/99, socket_rotation_total, socket_rotation_reasons, streaming_reconnect_total, streaming_reconnect_failures.
- Logs: structured event when rotation occurs with rotation_reason, conn_age_ms, in_flight_count, peer_ip.

Testing & benchmarks:
- Synthetic bench mixing 80% short (p50 30ms) / 20% long (continuous stream) workloads across 1000 RPS. Compare baseline vs hedging+rotation with/without priming.
- Chaos test: random connection stalls and DNS flaps, validate recovery and metrics.

Rollout:
- Feature flag gated. Start with a small cohort of internal customers (test tenants), monitor hedged_success_latency and token cost. If cost delta > 12% revert.

Open questions:
- Should hedging be allowed across model variants (e.g., primary cheaper model and fallback smaller model)? (Trade-off: consistency vs cost containment.)
- How to manage resume tokens for server implementations that do not provide them? Fallback to best-effort; requires docs.

Deliverables:
- TS SDK: hedging + rotation + streaming helper + tests + examples + telemetry
- Python & Go ports
- Bench reports and dashboard
- Docs + migration guide
comments: 2025-02-14: Initial design reviewed with Eng Networking. Agreed on hedging_window_ms default 60ms. Action: Arjun to prototype in TS SDK.
2025-02-20: Prototype (TS) PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-js-sdk/pull/4283. Basic hedging and rotation implemented, unit tests added.
2025-02-24: UX note from DX team (Elena): prefer a single config object (connectionSteward) instead of three separate flags. Will align across SDKs.

2025-02-28: Bench runs completed in staging: 99p latency reduced by 29% for short calls with hedging_enabled; token cost increased by 6.7%. Bench details: https://perf.redwood.ai/bench/hedging-2025-02-28
2025-03-03: Go port PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-go-sdk/pull/190. Needs review for ring buffer concurrency patterns.

2025-03-04: Security review triage: streaming resume tokens flagged for PII risk if user data echoed. Decided: SDK will not log resume payloads and will expose opt-in header behavior only when server indicates support.
2025-03-04: Next: consolidate TS config into connectionSteward object, add e2e chaos test for DNS flaps, and prepare rollout feature flag in console.
